newsitem.title: CANADA: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: North and Central America port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

CANADA Sept 9 - Halifax - All terminals operating normally. Container terminals no delays. Breakbulk piers have space. Bunker and tanker facilities no delays. Pier 9b closed indefinitely. Halifax shipyards and dartmouth marine slips available for repairs. Vancouver, BC, Sept 10 - GRAIN 3 vessels loading, 5 waiting, 1-2 days delay, 19 due 10-26/9. Delays will increase as new crop starts to arrive and shipping schedule becomes heavier. COAL (Roberts Bank) 2 vessels loading, 1 waiting, 19 due to load before 30/9. October schedule already lists 13 nominations/positions.

EL SALVADOR, Sept 6 - Acajutla - No vessels loading at berth, 2 discharging of which 1 cottonseed oil, 1 soy, no vessels waiting at anchorage. 9 Due by 3/10 of which 6 to discharge petroleum products, 2 containers, 1 bulk sulphate, 1 steel products, 1 ammonium sulphate), 1 to load bagged sugar, 1 to load/discharge containers, 1 to discharge general cargo which includes 40 containers.

HONDURAS, Sept 9 - Puerto Cortes - One vessel berthed discharging/loading containers, 1 vessel anchored to load bananas. 15 Vessels due of which 8 to discharge/load containers, 5 to load bananas, 1 to discharge containers/general cargo, 1 to discharge liquid chemicals. No berthing delays expected.

PANAMA, Sept 9 - Balboa - No vessels. Cristobal - Five vessels of which 1 lpg, 1 tanker, 1 reefer/general cargo, 1 container carrier, 1 passenger/ro/ro. Panama Canal - Repairs at Miraflores locks completed 6/9. Booking system remains at condition 2 (allocations reduced) until further notice, but traffic is expected to return to normal levels by 12/9. Lane outages will take place at Miraflores and Gatun locks from 29/9 until 6/10, with projected daily transits of 28-30 vessels. Delays during this period could be approx. 4 days, depending on vessel arrivals. Position 9/9, 38 vessels due, 43 in queue, 10 booked, 41 scheduled. 8/9 Actual arrivals 34, transits 38, average of booked and non-booked canal waters time 42.0 hours. Heavy rains and seasonal fog.

UNITED STATES, Sept 9 - Jersey City, NJ - No vessels in port. Port Newark, NJ - Two vessels in port. Port Elizabeth, NJ Five vessels in port. Perth Amboy, NJ - One vessel in port. Bayway, NJ - One vessel in port. Cartaret, NJ - One vessel in port. All northern New Jersey ports working normally, with no congestion/delays. Hampton roads, VA - Five general cargo/container vessels berthed and operating. 4 Vessels berthed loading coal, 4 anchored waiting to load, 2 bulkers loading fertiliser, 1 anchored waiting to load. 1 Bulker discharging manganese ore, 2 vessels berthed and under repair.

Baltimore, MD - Port working normally. Seven bulkers, 4 container vessels, 3 ro/ros, 2 auto vessels, 2 tankers, 3 general cargo. 2 Cable vessels on stand-by. 4 Vessels in repair yard. 5 Bulkers awaiting berths of which 2 to discharge sugar, 1 to load coal, 1 salt, 1 under arrest. East coast - Baltimore, MD - No congestion at Dundalk terminal anticipated this week. High winds expected in view of hurricane fran. No adverse conditions c.d canal/Baltimore harbour low ceiling. Elevators and coal operations working with no delays. Average waiting time consol coal 7 days. Liquid bulk facility operating normally. No berthing congestion. Anchorage clear at Baltimore and Annapolis.

Construction of new berth (no. 4) Seagirt commenced this week. Charleston, SC - The port of Charleston has suffered no damage from hurricane fran. The USCG closed the port as the storm approached, however this was lifted the next day as fran moved up the coast into Wilmington, NC. The only problem experienced at present is some heavy berth congestion as vessels try to make up time lost to the storm. New York, NY - No congestion at New York anchorages, none at container or tanker terminals. Congestion remains in Brooklyn sugar terminal. No congestion at Yonkers sugar terminal. Norfolk, VA - Norfolk southern coal pier expecting 16 vessels during this week. At present, 4 vessels are anchored waiting to load.

Dominion terminal is expecting 6 vessels. At present, 3 are anchored waiting to load. Pier ix coal terminal is expecting 3 vessels during the week. At present, there are no vessels anchored waiting to load. Due to hurricane fran, Norfolk southern coal pier stopped loadings at 22.00 hrs. 15/9. Dominion terminal stopped at 14.10 hrs. 5/9. Norfolk southern resumed about 15.00 hrs. 16/9. Dominion terminal and pier ix terminals experienced a severe power outage. Loadings should resume during the weekend. Cargill is not expecting any vessels during the coming week. Savannah, GA - Heavy congestion is expected at the Georgia ports authorities Garden City terminals and Ocean terminals through the week due to evacuation of the port caused by hurricane fran. Congestion is forecast to subside later in the week.

Many vessels were diverted and will enter again to complete cargo operations. All liquid bulk facilities are operating normally and no berth congestion is expected. Colonial marine terminals (bulk clay) expect a one or two day wait at anchorage for vessels. Weather is seasonal. Due to afternoon thundershowers, vessels with weather-sensitive cargo may expect some delays. All navigational conditions remain normal. Gulf coast - Houston, TX - No congestion at the city docks, public grain elevator and Cargill grain elevator. Some congestion at private terminals for breakbulk cargo. As usual, congestion at farmland grain elevator in Galveston. However, this has been reduced to approximately 2 days waiting. Mobile, AL - All private and state terminals continue to operate under normal conditions. No major weather problems in this area.

New Orleans, LA - It is normal for periods of rain to occur during the summer season and these conditions cause delays in cargo operations, especially grain loading. Grain shipments are slow, but normal for this season. River stage at 3.8 feet, normal transit times can be expected. Present max. permissable draft at S.W. Pass is 47 ft. Fresh water for vessels under 100,000 dwt., 46 Ft. Fresh water for vessels over 100,000 dwt. Some elevators are not working weekends due to slower than usual grain shipments. West coast - Columbia River - The Columbia River is experiencing increased grain vessel activity due to new September crop. There is a large movement of western white wheat bound for Pakistan throughout the month of September.

The Columbia River steamship operators association have formed a task force committee to review the current anchorage locations within the Columbia River district. They hope to look at potential anchorage locations within the port in preparation for vessel congestion in 1996/97. There are currently 15 grain vessels in the Columbia River district. Five of these vessels are loading, 10 are waiting. Average waiting period is 3-6 days. Coos Bay, OR - The past week has been slow. Three woodchip carriers loading. Cargo for Japan and one vessel currently loading. Linerboard for China discharge ports at Coos Bay dock. Log vessels appear to be somewhat slower for the month of September, with one vessel only on schedule to call Coos Bay.

However, imported (New Zealand) logs are scheduled to discharge in Coos Bay at Ocean terminal and another vessel carrying Mexican lumber also scheduled to call at Coos Bay mid-month. Glennbrook nickel terminal has 3 vessels scheduled to call during September and 5 woodchip vessels will call at woodchip terminals in Coos Bay. Long Beach, CA - Metropolitan (lb-212-214) - Looks moderately busy for the month of September. At present anticipate delays of 3-4 days at anchor awaiting berth. Koch carbon (lb-211) - 1 vessel at present scheduled for this month. Kaiser (la-49) - At present looks very busy (10-15 vessels) for the month. Coal/petcoke anticipated delays of up to 4-6 days waiting berth. The month of September looks moderately busy in the Los Angeles/Long Beach harbour for bulk cargoes.

San Francisco, CA - Pilots have just received new sounding data for the section of the transit above the S.P. Railroad bridge. Here are several shoaling places and the pilots have reduced the permissible transit to 29 feet +/- the existing tide at the time of transit. This will affect Stockton, Pittsburg, Antioch, Tosco Avon, Port Chicago, and Sacramento. Please note that the water in these areas is fresh. Seattle, WA - Currently no berthing congestion at Puget Sound grain elevators. Cargill updating equipment for faster elevation/cleaning of grain. Port Angeles and Seattle still offer lower bunker prices than Canaan west coast ports. Vancouver, WA - During the latter part of this week, rain has slowed the loading of grain. Waiting time for a grain berth is still approx. 2-3 Days.

No indication of the new grain crop season estimates as yet. Construction at Deltaport continues on schedule. Conditions Sept 10 - Honolulu, HI - Honolulu harbour - 3 Container vessels, 3 tugs and barges berthed, 1 tanker berthed for bunkers and provisions. 1 Passenger vessel berthed discharging passengers and bunkers. Offport anchorage - 1 Tanker anchored awaiting berth. Barbers Point harbour - 4 Tugs and barges berthed, 1 tanker berthed loading diesel. Offport moorings - 1 Tanker discharging crude oil.
